Where it began

Jamie Smith was born in Epsom on 12 July 2000. The 2005 Ashes caught his imagination, and at six or seven he was enrolled on a summer course at Sutton Cricket Club. By nine, while at primary school in Ewell, he was already in Surrey's development system.

He won a cricket scholarship to Whitgift School and was keeping wicket and making hundreds by the age of 12. He was a good footballer too, on AFC Wimbledon's books until he was 15, and he grew up a West Ham United supporter.

The player

His first-class debut, for Surrey against MCC in Dubai in March 2019, brought 127, making him the ninth Surrey batsman to score a hundred on debut and beating a county record for a debutant that went back to 1899. In 2022 he made his first double hundred, 234 not out against Gloucestershire, and he helped Surrey win the Championship in 2022 and 2023.

His Test debut came at Lord's on 10 July 2024 against the West Indies, and he made 70. Six weeks later at Old Trafford he made 111 against Sri Lanka for his first Test hundred, and he became only the third England player to pass 70 three times in his first five Test innings. In 2025 against India he made 184 not out, a new record score in Tests for an England wicketkeeper. By November 2026 he had played 25 Tests, scoring 1,549 runs at 39.72 with 2 hundreds and 10 fifties, and had taken 77 catches and 2 stumpings.

What made him special

Power, mostly. As a boy he was on the slight side, and he set out to build his strength; the result was a batter who could hit the ball a very long way. On an England Lions tour of Sri Lanka in February 2023 he reached a hundred in 71 balls, the fastest ever for the Lions. He has said that the attacking approach of Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes changed the way he thought about batting, and it shows.

Keeping wicket is patient, unseen work, and his 77 Test catches suggest he took to that side of it just as well.

Away from the middle

He joined Birmingham Phoenix in the Hundred in 2023 and that August signed a new long-term deal with Surrey. His first England cap came in an ODI against Ireland in September 2023. In 2024 the Professional Cricketers' Association named him their Men's Young Player of the Year, and he was one of Wisden's Cricketers of the Year in 2025.

And finally

Plenty of youngsters fell for cricket during that 2005 Ashes summer. Not many of them went on to keep wicket for England and set a record while doing it.
